system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Both STORM and Co-STORM are implemented in a highly modular way using [dspy](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy).
system_prompt_style.note: DSPy zero-shot signatures rendered per module with topic/perspective variables; paper: 'zero-shot prompting using the DSPy framework'.

env_context_strategy.note: Environment is a web/search corpus, not a repo; default is search-engine (keyword) retrieval; VectorRM gives embedding_rag as a config-reachable alternative.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Since it is usually impossible to fit the entireR within the context window of the LLM, we use the section title and headings of its all-level subsections to retrieve relevant documents from R based on semantic similarity
context_compaction.note: No history-shrinking processor described; context fitting done by retrieval selection, not compaction.

observation_format.evidence_quote: the LLM synthesizes the trustworthy sources to generate the answer ai, and these sources will also be added to R for full article generation

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Both STORM and Co-STORM are implemented in a highly modular way using [dspy](https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy).
tool_call_format.note: No tool-calling API; DSPy signature outputs (e.g. search queries) are parsed from text by the pipeline. Closest available value; see Ambiguities.

edit_primitive.note: No file-editing tool; output is an article, not code edits.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
STORM breaks down generating long articles with citations into two steps:

1. **Pre-writing stage**: The system conducts Internet-based research to collect references and generates an outline.
2. **Writing stage**
loop_primitives.note: Default is the fixed 4-module pipeline (research, outline, article, polish); simulated conversations are parallel per-perspective runs (multi_attempt-like). Co-STORM adds a turn-based discourse loop.

planning_granularity.note: The outline O is a stored artifact re-read by the article generation module; Co-STORM maintains a mind map.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: STORM simulates a conversation between a Wikipedia writer and a topic expert grounded in Internet sources
multi_agent_topology.note: Specialised LM roles (conv_simulator, question_asker, outline_gen, article_gen, article_polish) hand off in fixed sequence; Co-STORM is peer-like (experts + moderator).

delegation_mechanism.note: Control passes between configured LM roles within one pipeline run.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote:
runner.run(

    do_research=True,
    do_generate_outline=True,

human_in_loop.note: STORM runs unattended after topic input. Co-STORM (separate runner) supports user utterance injection: costorm_runner.step(user_utterance=...).

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Co-STORM also maintains a dynamic updated **mind map**, which organize collected information into a hierarchical concept structure
short_term_state.note: STORM keeps conversations, reference store R and outline as typed artifacts beyond messages.

long_term_memory.note: No cross-run memory described; each topic run starts from scratch.

self_verification.note: Polish stage is an LLM self-review pass; no tests/linters/judge in the pipeline.
